title: Closing the Loop: A Control-Theoretic Framework for Provably Stable Time Series Forecasting with LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2602.12756v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown exceptional potential in time series forecasting (TSF), leveraging their inherent sequential reasoning capabilities to model complex temporal dynamics. Existing approaches typically employ an autoregressive generation strategy to adapt LLMs for TSF. However, we identify a theoretical flaw in this paradigm: during inference, the model operates in an open-loop manner, recursively consuming its own generated outputs. translated_title: 闭环控制：一种可证明稳定的基于LLM的时间序列预测控制论框架
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）近年来在时间序列预测（TSF）中展现出卓越潜力，利用其固有的序列推理能力来建模复杂的时间动态。现有方法通常采用自回归生成策略来使LLMs适应TSF。然而，我们识别出该范式中的一个理论缺陷：在推理过程中，模型以开环方式运行，递归地消耗自身生成的输出。这导致误差累积，早期微小偏差在长时间范围内会级联成显著的滚动漂移。在本文中，我们从控制论的角度重新构建自回归预测，提出反馈驱动的LLM（F-LLM），一种新颖的闭环框架。与被动传播误差的标准方法不同，F-LLM通过一个可学习的残差估计器作为系统观测器，主动稳定轨迹。此外，我们提供了严格的数学证明，表明所提出的方法能保证预测稳定性。
tldr: 本文提出F-LLM，一种基于控制论的闭环预测框架，通过可学习残差估计器主动稳定LLM自回归预测轨迹，并提供了数学上的稳定性保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes F-LLM, a control-theoretic closed-loop forecasting framework that actively stabilizes LLM autoregressive prediction trajectories via a learnable residual estimator, with mathematical stability guarantees.
